title: Types of Motion
summary: Linear, circular, oscillatory and periodic: how to describe the way things move, and why a reference point matters.

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 5: Measurement of Length and Motion (types of motion)

objectives: I can explain that motion is a change in position relative to a reference point.
I can classify motion as linear, circular or oscillatory.
I can identify periodic motion and give examples.
misconceptions: An object is either moving or not, no matter who is watching (motion depends on the reference point).
Circular and oscillatory motion are the same.
